about: Experience archetypes: the page's structure and interaction model, rolled alongside paradigm, palette, fonts and genes. Sources: research notes 'Creative web beyond landing pages' (Oct 2026) and the six Tidewater reference builds. Library versions are the ones vendored for the showcase (GSAP 3.15.0, Lenis 1.3.26, Matter.js 0.20.0, three r186) or the npm versions the notes read on 2026-10-11. Recipes: references/experiences.md. Motion and media rules: references/motion-and-media.md.

fields.novelty_risk: risk that the archetype reads as a template or trend copy (high = sold as Framer templates or the default structure)
fields.effort: S = hours, M = a day or two, L = several days of build and tuning
fields.needs: what the brief must supply for the archetype to make sense; rolls penalise it when the sector does not match its fits
fields.motion_genes: motion personalities that suit it; roll.py moves the motion gene into this set when the paradigm allows (or away from 'still')
fields.showcase: path of the reference build relative to the showcase site root (x/<slug>/), null if none

experiences.name: Classic landing, well made
experiences.essence: A conventional, fast, scannable page: one clear hero, a few purposeful sections, one primary action, native scrolling throughout.
structure: hero that answers what / why / next in five seconds
proof: real product, numbers with sources, one quote
how it works: 3–5 steps or one live demo
objections or comparison
plans or the single offer
FAQ
closing action and footer
signature_moves: the genome's motif carried at 3–5 scales instead of per-section decoration
one orchestrated hero entrance (≤ 900 ms); everything else responds to the user
section rhythm from ground changes (bg / surface-2 / accent / inverted), not card grids
real product UI or real photography in the hero, cropped tight
experiences.interaction_model: Native vertical scroll; links, buttons and forms; no hijacked input.
techniques: CSS grid + container queries
CSS animation-timeline: view() reveals inside @supports, static end state as fallback
@starting-style for dialogs and menus
same-document View Transitions for tabs and plan toggles
hero with srcset/sizes and fetchpriority=high
libraries: optional: Motion 14.1 (npm 'motion') animate()/inView() for small UI motion

media.needs: One hero visual (product UI, photo or illustration) and 2–4 supporting visuals.
procedural: build the product UI in HTML/CSS and use it as the hero image
generative SVG pattern from the motif gene, written by a Python script with token colours
duotone any photo with CSS: grayscale image at mix-blend-mode: multiply on an accent ground

fits: regulated sectors: legal, finance, health, insurance
avoid_when: the brief asks for creative, playful, immersive or award-level work
the value is physical or sensory and can be shown rather than described
brand launches and campaigns where dwell time and shareability are the goal

novelty_risk.why: It is the structure every template ships. All distinctiveness must come from the genome (paradigm, palette, type, motif); the 'looks like a typical landing page' complaint is this archetype without a strong signature move.

experiences.mobile_strategy: Design the 390 px hero first; stack sections; a sticky bottom action only if it never covers focused content.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: Reveals become instant; hover lifts become colour changes; nothing depends on motion.
a11y_requirements: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: sticky header or action bar must not cover focus (scroll-padding)
2.5.8 Target Size: controls at least 24×24 CSS px (44 preferred)
2.3.3 Animation from Interactions: scroll reveals off under prefers-reduced-motion
1.4.10 Reflow at 320 CSS px

perf_budget.notes: LCP is HTML text or the hero image with fetchpriority=high; no JS needed before it.

experiences.name: Parallax scrollytelling
experiences.essence: A linear illustrated journey: each chapter is a pinned stage of depth layers whose timeline the reader scrubs, ending at the action.
structure: opening tableau (the one orchestrated entrance) with a scroll cue and a skip link to the action
4–7 chapters, each a pinned stage with its own scrubbed timeline
a progress trail that names the chapters and doubles as escape route
normal-scroll breathers between pins (facts, a quote, a photo)
the turn: the subject arrives at the reader (delivery, result)
the action (form, plans) in ordinary flow
footer
signature_moves: 8–10 SVG depth layers with depth-weighted travel (far layers barely move)
one object carried through every chapter (cherry → bean → bag)
SVG paths drawn by scroll (routes, rivers, steam)
a pinned stage where a real process plays out in order
a chapter trail that shows progress and jumps
experiences.interaction_model: Native vertical scroll scrubs pinned chapter timelines; chapter links jump; direction never changes.
techniques: GSAP ScrollTrigger pin + scrub (0.5–1 s catch-up), one timeline per chapter
gsap.matchMedia() desktop and mobile timelines; pins about 60% as long on phones
DrawSVG and MotionPath for routes and objects on paths
SplitText line masks for chapter titles
Lenis wheel smoothing with touch left native
IntersectionObserver-gated ambient video with a visible pause button
libraries: GSAP 3.15.0 + ScrollTrigger, SplitText, DrawSVGPlugin, MotionPathPlugin (all free since 3.13 under the Standard No-Charge License)

media.needs: Layered illustration per chapter (SVG), one ambient loop (water, mist, steam), optional photos for the breathers.
procedural: SVG depth layers generated in Python: smoothed random-walk ridges per layer, fills as var(--c-*) so the palette re-inks them
seamless water-caustic loop: numpy luma frames with integer time multipliers piped to ffmpeg (H.264 + VP9), laid over tokens with mix-blend-mode: soft-light
mist band: tileable noise WebP made seamless by cross-fading a shifted copy, drifted with transform

fits: food, drink and agriculture origin stories
subscription products with a supply chain
avoid_when: visitors need random access to facts (pricing, docs, support)
the story is thin: fewer than four real steps
no time to author per-chapter art for desktop and mobile

novelty_risk.why: Parallax is a decade-old trope and its only measured benefit is perceived fun (JUS 2015, n = 86). It reads fresh when the layers and the carried object come from the subject's own process.

experiences.mobile_strategy: Separate portrait artboards, pins about 60% as long, fewer moving layers; touch scroll stays native (Lenis syncTouch off).
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: No pins, no parallax, no autoplay: each chapter shows its composed end state as a still with its caption; the chapter trail still works.
a11y_requirements: 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions: parallax is the named non-essential example; off under reduce
2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide: ambient video longer than 5 s gets a visible pause button
2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: the fixed trail must not cover focused items
2.1.1 Keyboard: Space/PageDown and the chapter links reach every chapter
1.1.1 Non-text Content: illustrated stages aria-hidden, the story in real text beside them

perf_budget.notes: Showcase: GSAP core + ScrollTrigger + SplitText + DrawSVG + MotionPath ≈ 62 KB gz, Lenis 5 KB gz, water loop 316 KB H.264 / 241 KB VP9. Animate transform and opacity only; at most ~10 moving layers per pin.

experiences.needs: a real multi-step process or journey to narrate

experiences.name: Scroll-scrubbed sequence
experiences.essence: One hero object transforms frame by frame as the reader scrolls, with live data annotating each phase (the Apple-style reveal, driven by the subject's own numbers).
structure: static hero: the object at rest, headline, skip link (the poster frame is the LCP)
sticky sequence stage, 3–6 viewport heights, with phase beats as text
live readouts or a chart drawn in sync with the frames
the object lands in the next section (canvas hands over to an )
specs or comparison in normal flow
action
signature_moves: the object rides its own data (the bean rides its roast curve)
phase beats announced through a polite live region, debounced
progressive frame loading: every 32nd frame first, then fill in
a canvas-to-DOM hand-off when the sequence ends
experiences.interaction_model: Native scroll maps to a frame index; only the progress value is smoothed; nothing snaps.
techniques: canvas image sequence of 100–150 frames (desktop) and every other frame at half size (mobile)
ScrollTrigger progress → lerped value → drawImage only when the frame index changes
position: sticky stage instead of a JS pin
alternative: all-intra video (-g 1) scrubbed via currentTime, or WebCodecs with a sliding frame window
SVG chart built once in pixel space, then updated through attributes
poster still as LCP with fetchpriority=high
libraries: GSAP 3.15.0 + ScrollTrigger (or native scroll + one rAF loop)
scrolly-video picks WebCodecs, playbackRate or currentTime per browser (fails in iOS Low Power Mode)

media.needs: A frame sequence of the object changing: 3D render, turntable photos, filmed product or a procedural render.
procedural: numpy ray-cast or SDF render of the object per frame (ellipsoids + noise bump + simple lighting), saved as transparent WebP (quality ≈ 82, alpha_quality ≈ 85)
offline Blender/three.js render → PNG → WebP with PIL
all-intra MP4 + VP9 at the rendered size for the video variant
poster = frame 0 as WebP/AVIF ≤ 60 KB

fits: food and drink products: a bean, a bottle, a can
avoid_when: many SKUs, or a non-physical product such as SaaS (the reveal turns decorative)
the action would sit below a long pin with no skip link
iOS Low Power Mode matters and video scrubbing was chosen (it fails there; image sequences survive)

novelty_risk.why: The Apple reveal is widely copied. It is distinctive when the object's own data drives the overlay and the sequence goes somewhere (a landing, a hand-off), not when a product just spins.

experiences.mobile_strategy: Half-resolution frame set (≈ 640 px, every other frame), shorter stage, readouts stacked above the object.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: A static stepped sequence: 4–6 key frames as with their phase text, plus the whole chart as one SVG.
a11y_requirements: 2.3.3: the scrubbed transformation is off under reduce
2.2.2: an idle auto-spin longer than 5 s gets a pause control
4.1.3 Status Messages: phase changes via a polite live region, debounced about 700 ms
1.1.1: canvas aria-hidden; the stepped sequence and text carry the content
2.1.1: keyboard scrolling reaches every phase; a skip link jumps past the stage

perf_budget.notes: Showcase: 140 × 1200 px transparent WebP = 2.3 MB, 71 × 640 px = 0.9 MB. A decoded RGBA frame costs w × h × 4 bytes, so 148 decoded 1080p frames would need about 1.2 GB: rely on the browser's image cache or a sliding window, never hold them all as ImageBitmaps.

experiences.name: Physics playground
experiences.essence: The page is a box of things with mass: headline words, products and stickers fall, stack and can be flung, and playing earns something useful.
structure: the toy as hero: headline words drop in as bodies and settle into a readable line
a goal or counter that turns play into a reward (fill the grinder → the recipe opens)
an explicit controls row: drop, restack, pause, tilt
calm content in normal flow below (card pile, story, plans)
action
signature_moves: real DOM text as physics bodies, still selectable and translatable
a reward loop tied to the product (15 beans = one cup)
a draggable card pile with throw and inertia
phone tilt as gravity, opt-in
experiences.interaction_model: Pointer grab, drag and throw on canvas and DOM bodies; buttons give single-pointer alternatives; tilt opt-in on touch devices.
techniques: Matter.js bodies synced to DOM elements via transform each frame
small things drawn on one canvas from token-coloured sprites
fixed timestep with at most 3 substeps; enableSleeping; the loop stops when every body sleeps
IntersectionObserver + visibilitychange stop the loop
own pointer constraint (Matter's MouseConstraint listens to wheel events and can block page scroll)
GSAP Draggable + InertiaPlugin for the card pile
DeviceOrientation gravity behind a permission button
libraries: for 3D or hundreds of bodies: Rapier (SIMD npm builds, 2–5× faster than 2024 builds)

media.needs: Sprites of the subject's small things (beans, cans, stickers) and the headline font.
procedural: canvas-drawn sprites from tokens (radial gradient, stroke, highlight), rebuilt on 'unclaw:palette'
SVG stickers generated from the motif gene
no raster media needed

fits: playful consumer brands: snacks, coffee, toys, stationery
avoid_when: information density or quick scanning is the job
solemn or high-trust subjects (health, legal, finance)
very low-end mobile audiences (CPU cost per body)

novelty_risk.why: Falling-letter and sticker physics are a portfolio staple. It stays fresh when the physics demonstrates the product and play has a payoff.

experiences.mobile_strategy: Fewer bodies (about 90 instead of 180), larger touch hit radius, claim a touch only when it lands on a body so the page still scrolls, plus a tilt button.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: One composed still: bodies drawn at settled positions; the counter is replaced by a direct button ('Show the recipe').
a11y_requirements: 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: every drag outcome reachable by buttons (drop, restack, show recipe)
2.2.2: raining or moving bodies longer than 5 s need pause
2.5.4 Motion Actuation: tilt is opt-in and can be switched off
2.1.1: controls are real buttons; the reward dialog takes focus only when opened from the keyboard
4.1.3: counter milestones announced through a polite live region

perf_budget.notes: Matter 26 KB gz + GSAP/Draggable/Inertia ≈ 45 KB gz. DOM-synced bodies stay cheap below about 50; draw the rest on one sprite canvas; stop after about 20 quiet frames.

experiences.name: OS / desktop metaphor
experiences.essence: The site is an operating system: content lives in apps and documents opened as windows on a desktop, with menus, a Trash and a screensaver.
structure: a boot or login moment (≤ 1.5 s, skippable)
desktop: wallpaper, icons, a menubar where the brand is the system
a Welcome window open by default that says what this is and links the key apps
apps as content types: documents, a calculator, a video player, plans/checkout
system extras: Trash, Control Panel (sound, motion, text size), screensaver
phone: a home-screen shell where each app opens full screen
signature_moves: windows as accessible dialogs that move and resize by keyboard
a working menubar (roving focus, arrow keys, Escape)
content that only makes sense in the metaphor (a Trash you can restore from)
procedural dithered wallpaper and pixel sprites recoloured from tokens
a physics screensaver that stops on any input
experiences.interaction_model: Double-click or Enter opens apps; windows drag by the title bar and resize by a grip, both also by arrow keys; menus; phones get a tap-to-open home screen with history-backed back navigation.
techniques: window manager: z-order counter, focus on open, focus back to the opener on close
role=dialog + aria-labelledby per window; menus with role=menu and roving tabindex
pointer capture for drag and resize; keyboard nudge 16 px (Shift: 64 px)
history.pushState per open app on phones
localStorage for settings (sound, motion, text size)
16×16 sprite maps rendered as SVG path runs with token classes

media.needs: Icons, a wallpaper, one or two 'files' (a video, documents), UI sounds (off by default).
procedural: pixel sprites as 16×16 character maps → SVG <path> runs (Python or JS)
Bayer-dithered wallpaper drawn from tokens at runtime on a canvas
procedural pixel video: numpy frames → PNG → ffmpeg scale with flags=neighbor and -tune animation
grayscale video tinted with mix-blend-mode: multiply over a token ground

fits: AI or productivity products as a playground
avoid_when: mainstream audiences who need to find one thing fast
mobile-majority traffic without budget for a separate phone shell
deep content that would hide inside apps (findability, SEO)

novelty_risk.why: RetroOS, PixelOS and DIALUP.STUDIO are sold as Framer templates. It lands only when the apps are the subject's own tools and the metaphor is executed better than a template.

experiences.mobile_strategy: Phone home screen with an app grid and dock; apps open as full-screen sheets; the back button and an edge swipe close via history.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: No zoom-rectangle animations, no wallpaper parallax, screensaver shows a still frame; windows open instantly.
a11y_requirements: 2.1.1 / 2.1.2: every window, menu and icon operable by keyboard; Escape closes menus; no traps
2.5.7: move and resize have non-drag alternatives (arrow keys, zoom button, a Window menu)
2.4.3 Focus Order: focus moves into an opened window and back to its opener
2.4.11: windows never fully cover the focused element
4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: role=dialog/menu/menuitem with labels
1.4.2 Audio Control: UI sound off by default

perf_budget.notes: Showcase: ≈ 23 KB gz own JS + GSAP 28 KB + Matter 26 KB (screensaver, lazy-load it); pixel video 395 KB H.264. Keep every window's content in the HTML so it is indexable.

experiences.name: WebGL liquid / living material
experiences.essence: One full-screen simulated material (liquid, smoke, sand, ink) is the page's ground; the display type lives inside it and the visitor stirs it.
structure: the material at rest with display type rendered into it (DOM text kept underneath)
first pointer or touch stirs it; a one-line hint invites it
content sections slide over the material as scrims or panels
page choices feed the simulation (choosing a method pours milk)
the action panel above the material
signature_moves: type displaced by the material but always readable at rest
page choices change the material (hover a brew method, the cup changes)
token colours drive every pigment as uniforms; the palette customiser recolours the live simulation
adaptive quality: DPR steps down when frame time rises
experiences.interaction_model: Pointer and touch splat velocity and dye into the simulation; scroll moves a camera or crossfades scenes; a Pause button stops the loop.
techniques: WebGL2 ping-pong render targets: advect → curl/vorticity → divergence → Jacobi pressure (8–20 iterations) → gradient subtract
low-resolution velocity (≈ 112–144 px) with higher-resolution dye (640–1152 px)
one composite pass for lighting, caustics, scrims and type (a text atlas drawn from DOM glyph rects)
token colours → uniforms, refreshed on 'unclaw:palette'
pause on IntersectionObserver and visibilitychange; webglcontextlost → stills
libraries: OGL (≈ 29 KB min+gz in total) for small single-effect pages
three r186: three/webgpu + TSL compute for particles and fluids, with automatic WebGL2 fallback

media.needs: Posters and stills for LCP, reduced motion and no-WebGL; optional noise textures.
procedural: capture deterministic stills from the simulation itself (seeded random; preserveDrawingBuffer only in capture mode)
periodic FFT noise textures from numpy saved as 8-bit PNG
no video needed: the simulation is the media

avoid_when: low-end Android or software rendering is common in the audience (fill-rate bound)
the copy has to carry most of the message (the material competes)
no budget to tune both a simulation and its fallbacks

novelty_risk.why: A simulation of the subject's own material with type inside it is rare. A generic cursor-fluid trail on a dark page is not, so the material must come from the brief.

experiences.mobile_strategy: Smaller simulation tier (velocity 112, dye 640, 10 Jacobi iterations), DPR ≤ 1.5, touch splats only inside the stage so scrolling survives, controls docked in the thumb zone.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: Static stills captured from the simulation (one per state) with the same type and scrims; no loop at all.
a11y_requirements: 2.2.2: the material moves by itself for more than 5 s, so a visible Pause control comes early in tab order
2.3.1 Three Flashes: no strobing caustics or glints (at most 3 per second)
1.1.1: canvas aria-hidden; all text exists in the DOM (also for 1.4.12 Text Spacing and find-in-page)
1.4.3 Contrast: type over the material sits on a computed scrim
2.5.7: stirring is optional; every outcome reachable by buttons

perf_budget.notes: Full-screen passes are fill-rate bound: DPR ≤ 1.5; Jacobi iterations are the main cost dial; step DPR down by 0.25 when the frame-time average stays above ~26 ms for ~90 frames. Poster ≤ 60 KB WebP, preloaded.

experiences.name: Horizontal magazine
experiences.essence: An issue you turn sideways: vertical scroll drives a pinned track of spreads that follow print logic (masthead, contents, features, back cover).
structure: cover spread: masthead, cover lines, cover film or photo, issue and date
contents spread whose links jump to spreads
2–4 features as spreads: opener, photo essay, pull quote
a gatefold or interactive spread (kinetic words, a ticker)
back cover: the offer as a coupon or subscription
colophon
signature_moves: print production cues in CSS: misregistered second ink (multiply/screen), crop marks, folios
per-spread animations tied to the horizontal track (containerAnimation)
variable-font width and weight responding to scroll velocity
settling on two-page boundaries after scrolling stops
a token-tinted gradient-map cover video
experiences.interaction_model: Desktop: wheel, trackpad and arrow keys move a pinned horizontal track; contents links jump. Mobile: vertical snap pages. Reduced motion: stacked spreads.
techniques: GSAP ScrollTrigger pin + containerAnimation (the track tween uses ease: 'none')
Lenis smoothing + a debounced settle to page boundaries
SplitText line and character masks for headlines
registered custom properties (--wd, --wt) driving font-variation-settings
WebGL gradient-map shader over a grayscale video (dark → accent → paper)
gsap.matchMedia() with the horizontal mode gated on width, height and reduced motion
libraries: a variable display font with wdth and wght axes (the showcase uses Anybody)

media.needs: A cover loop or photo, 4–8 photographs for features, one variable display face.
procedural: seamless grayscale cover loop from periodic FFT noise (numpy) → ffmpeg, tinted live by a gradient-map shader from tokens
duotone/riso plates via SVG feComponentTransfer or CSS mix-blend-mode, inks from tokens
halftone via a CSS radial-gradient mask

avoid_when: task-oriented visitors (NN/g: horizontal scrolling is poorly discovered and costly to operate)
long reading text inside the moving track
mobile-majority audiences without the vertical version

novelty_risk.why: Horizontal-scroll sections are common. A full print-logic issue with registration, folios and a real contents page is rarer, but the gimmick wears off if the spreads lack editorial content.

experiences.mobile_strategy: Vertical scroll-snap pages (a spread becomes one or two screens), no pin, display words fitted to the viewport by measuring their narrowest and widest wdth.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: Spreads stack vertically as one long page; no pin, no velocity type; the cover video waits behind a play button.
a11y_requirements: 2.1.1: arrow keys and Space move the track; contents links reach every spread
2.5.7: prev/next buttons or contents links as single-pointer alternatives
2.2.2: cover film and ticker each get a pause control
1.4.10 Reflow: the vertical mobile version is the reflow
2.4.11: fixed folios and navigation never cover focused links

perf_budget.notes: Showcase: cover 1.5 MB H.264 / 403 KB VP9 at 1280×720; photos 210–445 KB JPEG (serve AVIF/WebP in production). Font-axis animation reflows text each frame, so keep it to a few words.

experiences.name: Scroll-driven 3D world
experiences.essence: The page is one continuous 3D scene and scrolling moves a camera along an authored path; sections are places, not stacked blocks.
structure: arrival shot: HTML headline over a poster frame; the canvas fades in after LCP
4–6 stations along a camera spline, each with a DOM text card
a transition through a portal or tunnel between acts
one interactive station (particles form the links, an object to inspect)
exit into normal HTML: content, links, action
signature_moves: camera on a spline with eased dwell at stations
one material language, baked lighting and AO
DOM text cards anchored to 3D positions
quality presets by GPU tier, plus a list-view escape
experiences.interaction_model: Scroll drives camera progress; optional pointer parallax on the camera (capped); stations reachable from a fixed nav.
techniques: three.js: WebGLRenderer + GLSL, or three/webgpu + TSL with its WebGL2 fallback
scroll progress (ScrollTrigger or Lenis) → CatmullRomCurve3.getPointAt(t)
Blender → glTF → gltf-transform optimize (meshopt, KTX2, textures ≤ 2048 px)
InstancedMesh / BatchedMesh, baked lighting, at most ~3 dynamic lights
detect-gpu tiers + a frame-time monitor that steps DPR
render loop paused off-screen and on hidden tabs
libraries: React Three Fiber 9.x if the site is React

media.needs: A modelled world (Blender or Spline), baked textures, one poster frame per station.
procedural: procedural terrain and props from noise in three.js; the palette as a small token-coloured gradient texture
station posters rendered once offline or captured from the canvas → AVIF/WebP
an SVG 2.5D version of the world as the no-WebGL fallback

avoid_when: B2B lead generation or support (people need information fast)
no 3D artist or time to build and optimise assets
text would live only in WebGL (SEO, screen readers)

novelty_risk.why: Award-tier and hard to template (Igloo Inc, Awwwards SOTY 2024). The risk is cost and performance, not sameness.

experiences.mobile_strategy: Low-quality preset (no post-processing, smaller shadows, DPR 1–1.5), a shorter camera path, stations as full-screen cards; tier-0 GPUs get the poster story.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: No fly-through: one static frame (or poster) per station beside its DOM card; scrolling is ordinary.
a11y_requirements: 2.3.3: camera fly-throughs removed under reduce
2.2.2: idle ambient motion longer than 5 s can be paused
2.1.1 + 2.4.3: stations reachable by keyboard through DOM nav; focus moves the camera, without fast motion under reduce
1.1.1: canvas aria-hidden or labelled; hotspots are real buttons
2.4.11: fixed canvas and UI layers never cover focus

perf_budget.notes: LCP is HTML or the poster; the 3D bundle loads after load/idle. Vendor estimates: shader compile 50–300 ms each, large texture upload 50–200 ms each, so pre-compile during loading.

experiences.name: Explorable 3D scene
experiences.essence: Content lives as objects in a small navigable space (a desk, a room, an island, a ring of projects); you pick things up instead of reading a menu.
structure: the scene at rest with a short instruction and a 'list view' toggle
objects as sections, each with a hover and focus label
selecting an object moves the camera and opens its DOM panel
a deep-linkable URL per object
persistent nav: overview, list view, contact
signature_moves: object as navigation (an isometric desk, a project ring)
a camera move that turns the selected object into its detail page
characters or props that react to the visitor
a list view with the same content for scanning
experiences.interaction_model: Point or tap objects (raycast on low-poly proxies), orbit or pan within limits; Tab cycles DOM proxies for each object.
techniques: three.js scene with invisible low-poly raycast proxies
DOM buttons positioned over 3D objects for focus and screen readers
GSAP camera tweens between saved poses
a URL per object (history.pushState)
Spline or Blender → glTF → gltf-transform

experiences.name: Infinite canvas / looping gallery

structure: the canvas or loop filling the viewport with a one-line intro
drag or scroll to explore; hover or focus a tile for its title
open a tile → detail view (tile morphs into the hero)
a toggle between canvas and index list (sortable, filterable)
about and contact fixed in a corner
signature_moves: modulo wrapping so the plane never ends
velocity-reactive distortion on tiles (WebGL planes or capped CSS skew)
a shared-element transition from tile to detail
two viewing modes, as PHOTOYOSHI does
experiences.interaction_model: Pointer drag with inertia, wheel and trackpad pan, arrow-key panning; Enter opens a tile; the index view serves keyboard and screen-reader users.

GSAP Draggable + InertiaPlugin, or Observer for wheel/touch intent
WebGL plane per image with a velocity uniform (OGL or three), or CSS skew
same-document View Transitions for tile → detail
IntersectionObserver-driven lazy decoding

experiences.name: Interactive documentary / comic
experiences.essence: A story told in panels and media pieces (frames, maps, data, clips) that scroll advances one beat at a time, using print or film grammar.
structure: title page, with content notes if needed
chapter openers as full-bleed panels
panel sequences: 1–3 panels per screen, captions and speech as real text
inserts: a map that draws, a chart that builds, a short muted clip
an optional choice or interactive panel per chapter
credits and sources, then the action (donate, visit, subscribe)
signature_moves: panel borders and gutters as the grid; panels that break their frames
captions set in the display face, speech in DOM bubbles
scroll-snapped beats inside the story section only
one recurring visual device (a colour, a character) carrying continuity
experiences.interaction_model: Native scroll with proximity snapping per beat; panel animations play on entry; next and previous beat buttons.
techniques: CSS scroll-snap-type: y proximity inside the story section only
animation-timeline: view() panel reveals (Chrome, Safari) with a static fallback (Firefox)
ScrollTrigger toggleActions or IntersectionObserver to play and pause clips and maps
SVG maps drawn with DrawSVG or stroke-dashoffset
speech bubbles as positioned DOM elements, never baked into images
libraries: GSAP 3.15.0 + ScrollTrigger + DrawSVGPlugin for maps and choreographed panels

media.needs: Illustrated panels, maps, short clips, an optional soundtrack (off by default).
procedural: panels built as SVG/HTML illustration from token-coloured shapes (flat or line illustration genes)
halftone or riso treatment of photos with PIL or CSS masks
map paths from GeoJSON, simplified in Python and written as SVG

avoid_when: the audience wants random access
there is no real story or script
content changes weekly (panels are costly to redraw)

novelty_risk.why: Comics and documentaries are authored work; the risks are thin storytelling and poor mobile panel layouts, not sameness.

experiences.mobile_strategy: One panel per screen in reading order, captions above the art, proximity snapping (never mandatory) so fast readers are not trapped.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: Panels appear without movement; clips become click-to-play; maps render complete.
a11y_requirements: 1.1.1: every panel's alt text carries its beat; speech is real text
1.2.2 Captions and 1.2.3/1.2.5 audio description (or a transcript) for clips
2.2.2: auto-playing clips longer than 5 s can be paused
2.4.6 Headings and Labels: chapter headings plus a chapter index
2.3.3: panel motion off under reduce

perf_budget.notes: Lazy-load panels and clips per chapter; content-visibility: auto on chapters that are not animating; reserve aspect-ratio on every panel.

a key in plain language

method and sources
action (download, share your version, subscribe)

the brand mark itself drawn by the system
annotations that point into the generated image

seeded PRNG (mulberry32, xorshift) from a URL parameter

checkout or reservation; specs and delivery facts below

every configuration has a URL (shareable, indexable)
constraints explained inline (why an option is unavailable)
compare or undo the last change

novelty_risk.why: Index lists with hover thumbnails are a portfolio staple; distinctiveness comes from the metadata design, the type and the view transitions.

experiences.mobile_strategy: List first with taller rows, filters in a sheet, small inline images instead of hover thumbnails.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: View switches without morphing (instant or a crossfade); thumbnails appear without follow motion.
a11y_requirements: 1.3.1: list or table semantics; filters as a labelled form
4.1.3: result counts announced
2.4.3: focus stays on the filter after an update
1.4.13: hover thumbnails also on focus and dismissible
2.1.1 / 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts: single-key shortcuts can be turned off and never fire while typing

perf_budget.notes: Filtering under 50 ms for 500 items; lazy thumbnails with fixed aspect-ratio; the list text is the LCP.

experiences.name: Kinetic poster / one screen
experiences.essence: A single-screen typographic poster that moves: one message set enormous and animated through the type itself (axes, masks, marquees), with one action.
structure: one screen: the message as moving type
secondary facts (date, place, price) as small fixed type
one action (tickets, RSVP, download)
optional second screen with details in plain text
footer line
signature_moves: variable-font axes animated through registered custom properties
masked line reveals that resolve into a still, legible poster within 1.5 s
one or two marquee bands with a pause control
type that answers pointer or scroll velocity (capped)
experiences.interaction_model: Mostly watched; pointer or scroll nudges the type; the action is always visible.
techniques: @property-registered --wght/--wdth animated by keyframes or animation-timeline
SplitText masks (lines, chars) with autoSplit and its default ARIA handling
CSS marquee: duplicated track, translateX(-50%), paused by a real button
text-box trim for exact cap alignment (Chrome 133, Safari 18.2, Firefox 154)
libraries: a variable display font with expressive axes

media.needs: A variable display font; optionally one texture or photo.
procedural: poster texture from numpy noise (grain, halftone) → PNG/WebP ≤ 60 KB
an MP4 of the poster for social, captured headless and encoded with ffmpeg

avoid_when: the page must hold a lot of information
body-text-heavy content
the brand typeface is timid or not variable

novelty_risk.why: Marquees and split-text reveals are trend staples; it stands out when the type motion encodes the message (weight grows with the countdown, width with the crowd).

experiences.mobile_strategy: Recompose for portrait (fewer words per line, narrower wdth so words fit), action in the thumb zone.
experiences.reduced_motion_strategy: The final poster frame, static; marquees stopped; axis changes only as instant hover/focus states.
a11y_requirements: 2.2.2: marquees and loops longer than 5 s need a pause control (pausing only on hover does not count)
2.3.1: no strobing type
1.4.4 Resize Text and 1.4.10 Reflow: poster type uses clamp() and reflows
split text keeps its accessible name (SplitText aria: 'auto')

perf_budget.notes: Font-axis animation reflows every frame: limit it to the headline; preload the display font and use font-display: optional or a metric-matched fallback.
